label: Confirmed Deaths
source: Government/Defensoría del Pueblo tallies (as of Jul 9, 2026)
contestNote: Union and independent sources dispute how many deaths are directly attributable to blockade-caused hospital shortages (~14 of the total) versus other causes.

label: State of Emergency
value: Decree 5707 (90-day extension) awaiting ALP vote, Sep 16; govt floats possible estado de sitio
source: Government of Bolivia / Defense Minister Ernesto Justiniano, Sep 14-16, 2026
contestNote: COB calls the extension "an attack on democracy"; the Morales-aligned CSUTCB has declared "permanent mobilization" against it; the government disputes it and cites ongoing mobilization risk.
deltaNote: The cabinet formally approved Decree 5707 on Sep 14, extending the state of exception (in force since Jun 20) by 90 more days; the decree was sent to the Legislative Assembly Sep 15, and VP Lara convened a plenary session for Sep 16 at 16:00 to vote on it before the original term lapses around Sep 18-19. COB executive secretary Mario Argollo called an extension "un atentado a la democracia," and the CSUTCB declared "estado de emergencia y movilización permanente" Sep 15, setting a Sep 26 national assembly in Lauca Ñ to plan its response. Political blocs remain split: Súmate and a PDC faction signal likely support, while Libre and COD Chuquisaca oppose. Separately, presidential spokesperson José Luis Gálvez said Sep 16 the government could escalate further to a state of siege, including possible curfews, if new blockades materialize.

label: Active Blockades
value: 0 confirmed active; moto-taxi 'recess' to Oct 10; govt warns of estado de sitio if blockades resume
source: La Razón / FM La Paz, Sep 11, 2026; Infobae, Sep 16, 2026
deltaNote: San Pablo bridge (Marbán province, Beni) blockade was lifted Aug 30 after a 4-day standoff, with the government pledging Bs. 9.80/L diesel capped at 120L weekly for the province. Seven Santa Cruz moto-taxi federations set an indefinite blockade at 13+ points for Sep 11 over fuel shortages and price increases, then called it off after overnight talks with Hydrocarbons Minister Marcelo Blanco and YPFB — organizers call it a 'recess,' not a resolution, and set Oct 10 as their checkpoint. Yapacaní's status as of Sept 3 was unconfirmed since; Decree 5676's Bs. 18/liter large-consumer tier remains unrepealed. No blockades were confirmed active as of Sep 16, but presidential spokesperson José Luis Gálvez said the same day the government could declare a state of siege, with possible curfews, if new mobilizations start, and the Morales-aligned CSUTCB declared 'permanent mobilization' Sep 15 against the state-of-exception extension, planning a Sep 26 national assembly to set its next moves.

label: USD Exchange Rate (floated)
source: Central Bank of Bolivia (official TCO, Sep 15, 2026)
deltaNote: Rate climbed further from Sep 4's Bs. 12.45 to a new record Bs. 12.655 around Sep 9-10, then eased for five straight sessions — Bs. 12.42 (Sep 10), Bs. 12.04 (Sep 11), Bs. 11.53 (Sep 12), continuing down to Bs. 10.99 by Sep 15 — after the BCB suspended new dollar-purchase operations (Sep 7), created a Restricted Monetary Reserve under Resolution RD Nº 131/2026 (Sep 8), and began direct dollar distribution to private financial-system entities (Sep 9) to curb what it called 'unnecessary shocks' in the currency market. A parallel-market gap persists (Bs. 11.77-11.87 on Sep 14 versus the day's Bs. 11.53 official rate). Still up from the 15-year peg of Bs. 6.96 before the Jun 29 float.

label: Inflation (y/y)
contestNote: The IMF forecasts full-year 2026 inflation near 20.7%, but Bolivia's statistics institute (INE) reported an official year-on-year print of just 4.93% for July 2026 — pass-through from the June currency float and December fuel-subsidy cuts had not yet fully hit consumer prices.

label: Diesel Price — Large Consumers (GRACOS)
deltaNote: Up from the prior Bs. 9.80-9.90/L rate; the subsidized Bs. 9.80/L price is unchanged for transport operators and individual consumers
contestNote: Facing backlash over the 84% hike, Deputy Hydrocarbons Minister Hernán Paredes said Aug 25 the decree "has to be modified" toward a more competitive price. But Minister of the Presidency Fernando Aramayo rejected repeal on Aug 27, attributing the decree to IMF conditionality; new blockades against it began Aug 26 in Beni and Oruro. New Economy Minister Christian Morales Burgos, sworn in Aug 25 replacing interim minister Óscar Mario Justiniano, said Aug 26 the decree needs adjustments "to minimize risks" from producer mobilizations; the Pro Santa Cruz Civic Committee set a 72-hour ultimatum (deadline Sun Aug 30) to repeal it before escalating to a region-wide Asamblea de la Cruceñidad.

label: Arrests (crisis-related)
contestNote: MAS-aligned and union groups characterize a portion of arrests and the Evo Morales warrant as politically motivated prosecution.

label: Cerimedo-Linked Detentions
value: 4 held + 1 arrest ordered; Cerimedo faces 4 investigations
source: Attorney General Roger Mariaca / Infobae, Sep 9, 2026
deltaNote: Attorney General Roger Mariaca announced Sep 9 that prosecutors added usurpation-of-functions and money-laundering charges to Cerimedo's illicit-enrichment case, bringing his concurrent legal exposure to four matters: illicit enrichment/money laundering, attempted femicide against Nadia Beller, domestic violence, and the Beni drug-trafficking-flights probe opened in late August. Beller was summoned Sep 12 (with businessman Robin Jofré Azzarini) as a witness in the illicit-enrichment case; because she cannot travel to La Paz for health reasons, her testimony will be taken via advance-proof procedure in Santa Cruz. She expanded her declaration Sep 9, alleging Cerimedo "coordinated with law enforcement forces" during his informal advisory role. Cerimedo remains held at the high-security Chonchocoro facility after transfer from Palmasola.

label: YPFB State Intervention
source: Government of Bolivia, Supreme Decree 5697, Sep 2, 2026
deltaNote: President Paz placed state oil company YPFB under "extraordinary, transparent and temporary" intervention for up to 180 days (extendable once by 90), via a commission of the Economy, Production/Environment/Water, Hydrocarbons/Energy and Public Works ministries, to audit the fuel import/distribution chain and trace smuggling and diversion networks. The decree does not dissolve YPFB or change its legal status.
